name: requirement_quotes
description: The customer's own words behind a requirement — one row per thing a customer said, with the quote, the date, the stage they were at and what happened to the deal. This is the evidence view: use it whenever a theme from requirement_lost_value or customer_objection_themes is about to be quoted to a person, and for 'what did customers actually say about X', 'show me the quotes', 'give me examples'. Always name the deal a quote came from so it can be checked. is_objection marks the ones the extraction read as pushback rather than a neutral request. Note these are extracted snippets, not whole messages — a quote can read more bluntly out of context than it did in the thread, so prefer several quotes over one when characterising a theme. requirement_label is the raw extracted wording; requirement_theme is the grouped version. ALWAYS identify a deal by deal_name, never by opportunity_id. The id is in the data so a row can be looked up, not so it can be shown — an answer that reads "2lVBs41TxfmKK8U03fIn said the price was too high" is unusable to a rep, who cannot tell which customer that is without searching for the id. Say the deal name, and the owner when it helps.

params.name: deal
params.description: Only rows on deals whose name contains this text. Prefer this over opportunity_id — a rep knows the name.

params.name: requirement
params.description: Only quotes under requirement themes matching this text.

params.name: quote_contains
params.description: Only quotes containing this text. Use to confirm a theme really says what its name claims.

params.name: stage
params.description: Only things said while the deal was at this stage.

params.name: objections_only
params.description: true for objections only, false for neutral requirements only.

params.name: opportunity_id
params.description: Everything a single deal's customer asked for.
